newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Dec 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Beijing clarified recent rumours in Hong Kong that China would open the A-share markets to foreign investors early next year.
-- China's Futures and Securities Commission's spokesman said that its policy of stably developing its stock market had not changed despite recent calls for crackdown on stock market speculation.

-- SING TAO -- China had started to control the media's influence on the stock market. A market commentary programme on CCTV had been cancelled, while the next step would be to rectify the financial publications.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Because of a lack of funds, China would reduce its military force by one million staff during the ninth five-year-plan period and concentrate on technology development.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Police Commissioner Eddie Hui said it was difficult to solve cross-border commercial crime because of the different banking and legal systems in China and Hong Kong. But the head of China Central Bureau of Interpol said that China would strengthen its efforts to crackdown on commercial crimes in the two places and would not allow criminals to shelter in Hong Kong and Macau.
-- MING PAO -- Financial research showed that the average family spare money in Chinese cities and towns was close to 30,000 yuan.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Chinese Premier Li Peng had approved the fourth lot of 27 state enterprises to seek listing overseas. The name list would be announced shortly.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A U.S. customs team had made a confidential visit to the territory to inspect records on textile shipments. The visit was intended to match export and import data.

-- A consortium of 10 foreign banks led by Standard Chartered Bank on Tuesday introduced a novel financing arrangement for power plants in China when they sealed a deal to provide US$124 million for a Shanghai power company.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa condemned Britain and the Hong Kong govennment for ignoring the reality of the provisional legislature.
